first.text: At the Last Crossing table read, the brother's second call felt repetitive. Three readers started turning pages before the daughter finished speaking, which is a useful sign that the scene had already made its point. Save their timing notes beside the read recording, with the long hesitation marked rather than trimmed out. Dax thought that pause gave the daughter time to decide whether she trusted her brother, so it should survive the edit. Cut the second call from the next screenplay draft and move its one new fact into the first call. Try the brother's admission immediately after she describes the empty landing; then let her answer with a small practical question. Keep the read's original scene numbers in the notes so we can still find the comments after renumbering the draft.

first.text: Make the compact-keyboard and close-mouse positions comfortable first, then photograph them for my shared-desk reset card. I tried moving the mouse inward while keeping the wide keyboard, but my hand kept hitting the number pad. The smaller keyboard gives that space back without changing the desk itself. Check the cable slack at the new position; yesterday it pulled the mouse toward the back corner halfway through editing. Rui needs a separate picture showing the larger keyboard, because the number pad is useful for their work. We should each do a reset from the other person's arrangement, using only the pictures, and note anything that requires guessing. Put the unused keyboard in the side cubby with its connector visible. The handover should preserve both workable arrangements even when we swap during a short lunch break.
